subject: general
question: Which of the following is true about action and reaction forces according to Newton’s third law?

options.text: They act in the same direction on the same object
They act on the same object at different times
They act on two different objects at the same time
They cancel each other out because they act on one object

solution:
The correct answer is __**They act on two different objects at the same time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion** states that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. This law describes the nature of **forces** between interacting objects.
 
• Action and reaction forces always occur in **pairs**. A single, isolated force cannot exist in nature.
 
• A fundamental characteristic of these force pairs is that they **act on two different objects**. If object A exerts a force on object B, then object B simultaneously exerts a force back on object A. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The forces act in **exactly opposite directions**. Statement 1 claims they act in the same direction, which contradicts the law. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• These forces are **simultaneous**, meaning they exist at the **exact same moment**. There is no **time delay** between the action and its reaction. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
